part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Confirm the invention lands in a statutory class
check: Verify the draft's claimed subject matter can be reasonably classified as a process/method (including a new use), machine, article of manufacture, or composition of matter.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Screen the claims against the judicial exceptions
check: Verify no independent claim, read as a whole, amounts to a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea.
applies_to: all applications; especially software, business method, diagnostic, chemical/biotech

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Software: verify the draft shows "something more" than a general-purpose computer
check: Verify the specification and claims identify a technological problem in the computer or the Internet that the software solves, rather than a conventional computerized implementation of a known task.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Make the claims recite the unconventional nature of the process or machine
check: Verify that where eligibility rests on unconventionality (special-purpose or embedded computer, non-conventional process rules), the *claims* — not just the specification — call that unconventionality out.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Business methods: reframe around the technological hurdle
check: Verify a business-derived invention is framed in terms of technological hurdles overcome, not as a fundamental economic practice or a method of organizing human activity.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Rule out the classic non-statutory categories
check: Verify the claimed subject matter is not a purely mental process, printed matter without an instrumentality, a naturally occurring thing, an idea per se, a bare algorithm, or a transitory signal.
note: a script can flag the tell-tale language (signal, carrier wave, printed matter) but the mental-process and natural-product calls need a model

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Naturally occurring subject matter: check for the human-made hook
check: Verify that any claim reading on a natural product, gene, plant, or organism recites human-made structure, a purified/synthetic form, or a new use, rather than the natural thing itself.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Verify the specification states a specific, realistic use
check: Verify the specification affirmatively recites at least one functional (not aesthetic) use for the claimed invention, stated concretely enough to be proved if challenged.
applies_to: all applications; critical for chemical and pharmaceutical
note: a script can locate candidate utility sentences; whether the use is specific and provable is judgment

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Aesthetic-only inventions: add a functional purpose or redirect to a design application
check: Verify the invention's asserted advantage is not purely aesthetic; if it is, confirm a utility application is the right vehicle at all.
applies_to: all applications; industrial design, housings, screen graphics

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Operability: verify the draft will not read as inoperative
check: Verify the disclosure describes a mechanism that a technically trained examiner will accept as workable and that does not appear to violate an accepted physical law.
applies_to: all applications; energy, perpetual motion, esoteric physics, medical claims

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Theoretical phenomena: require a claimed hardware-based application
check: Verify the draft claims a practical, realistic, hardware-based application rather than the underlying discovered phenomenon or principle.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Legality, safety, and the statutory exclusions
check: Verify the invention is not solely useful for illegal purposes, is not an unsafe drug, is not a nuclear weapon, is not a tax-avoidance strategy, and is not a human organism — and that any legitimate use is the one the draft describes.
note: FDA/safety status for a drug case is an intake fact, not readable from the draft

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Identify and record at least one physical or method-step difference over the closest prior art
check: Verify the file contains an explicit statement of what the claimed invention has that the closest prior-art references do not.
note: a script can assemble the claim-element vs reference grid; the mapping itself is a model call

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Do not mistake new results for novelty
check: Verify the asserted novelty is an actual hardware or method-step difference, not merely an advantage such as lighter, faster, safer, or cheaper.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Apply the single-reference rule and look for a complete anticipating disclosure
check: Verify no single prior-art reference shows all of the claimed features operating the same way for the same purpose.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Verify the prior-art search covered the full statutory universe
check: Verify the search was not limited to in-force U.S. patents, English-language sources, or patent literature.
note: overlaps Part B (B06); kept with the threshold gate because it feeds the §102 conclusion

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Account for secret prior art in the risk assessment
check: Verify the applicant has been told that a clean search does not guarantee clean prior art, because unpublished pending applications are already prior art as of their effective filing dates.
applies_to: all applications; crowded and fast-moving fields
note: verifies the applicant was advised about secret prior art — an advisory fact, not a property of any document

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Check derivation risk and the common-assignee / joint-research exception
check: Verify whether anyone else may have filed first on the same invention and, if so, whether derivation or the common-assignee/joint-research-agreement exception applies.
note: who else had access, common assignment, and any joint research agreement are intake facts

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Check for abandonment of the invention
check: Verify the inventor did not consciously give up on the invention at some point before deciding to file.
note: cannot be verified from documents at all — requires the project chronology and the inventor's intent

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Date every disclosure that came from the inventor and confirm the one-year deadline
check: Verify the intended filing date is within one year of the earliest disclosure of the invention by the inventor or by anyone who obtained the details from the inventor.
note: date arithmetic is mechanical once the disclosure list exists, but the list itself comes only from the inventor

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Confirm no third-party disclosure predates the filing date — there is no grace period for those
check: Verify that no public disclosure, use, sale, or knowledge originating from anyone other than the inventor occurred before the intended filing date.
note: third-party public use or knowledge is rarely discoverable from documents — requires interviewing the inventor

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Date any public use or unrestricted showing
check: Verify whether the invention has been used or shown publicly without restriction, and when.
note: requires an inventor interview about demos, beta users, house showings and installed prototypes

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Date any offer to sell, sale, or commercial use
check: Verify whether the invention or a product embodying it has been offered for sale, sold, or commercially used, and confirm the filing date beats the applicable bar.
note: offers, quotes and pre-orders are intake facts; the one-year computation is then mechanical

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Confirm foreign filing rights have not already been destroyed
check: Verify whether any marketing, use, sale, or showing occurred before filing, and record that foreign-filing rights may already be gone.
applies_to: all applications where non-U.S. protection is wanted
note: depends on whether foreign protection is wanted, which only the client can say

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Experimental use: confirm the exception actually applies and that filing precedes commercial use
check: Verify that any pre-filing public use claimed as experimental was bona fide experimental, and that no nonexperimental use has begun.
applies_to: all applications; field-tested and outdoor-installed inventions
note: whether a use was bona fide experimental turns on contemporaneous records the inventor must supply

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Statutory bars and the grace period (dated checks)
title: Check the inventor's own earlier foreign filings and priority chain
check: Verify whether the inventor has an earlier foreign application or patent, and confirm the U.S. filing date is set to preserve both validity and priority.
applies_to: applications with foreign-origin inventors or earlier foreign filings
note: the two one-year computations are mechanical; knowing an earlier foreign filing exists is an intake fact

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Confirm the novel feature produces a new and unexpected result
check: Verify that the difference between the claimed invention and the prior art produces a result that would be unexpected or surprising to a person having ordinary skill in the art.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Screen the claims for predictable substitutions and changes in degree
check: Verify the claimed advance is not a mere substitution of equivalents, a change in form, size, material, or degree, a duplication of parts, or the addition of modern electronics, without an unexpected result.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Combination inventions: test for synergism, not aggregation
check: Verify a combination of individually old elements produces results greater than the sum of the elements' separate results.
applies_to: all applications; combination and kit inventions, chemical mixtures, recipes

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Pre-build the anti-KSR combination argument
check: Verify the draft supports an argument that the prior-art references would not have been combined, given that KSR requires only some apparent reason to combine.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
title: Inventory the secondary factors before filing
check: Verify the applicant has worked through the secondary indications of nonobviousness and identified every one that applies.
applies_to: all applications; essential where the new and unexpected results are marginal
note: several secondary factors (others failed, long-felt need, commercial success) are facts only the applicant can supply

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: Make the specification state the new and unexpected results explicitly
check: Verify the specification tells the examiner, in words, what unexpected result the novel feature produces — not just what the invention is.
note: a script can surface candidate unexpected-result passages; sufficiency is a model call

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: New-use inventions: confirm process claiming and an unexpected result
check: Verify that an invention presented as a new use of old hardware is claimed as a process and is supported by a genuinely different use producing new, unexpected results.
note: claim statutory form is mechanically detectable; whether this is a new-use invention is not

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: Test claim breadth for design-around before filing
check: Verify the claims are not so narrow or so easy to design around that a granted patent would be commercially worthless.

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: Strip inventor-status and manner-of-invention arguments from the draft
check: Verify the draft does not rest any patentability argument on who the inventor is, their credentials, or how much effort the invention took.
note: a script can flag credential and effort language in the background/summary; a model decides if it is load-bearing

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: Resolve open legal questions rather than assuming
check: Verify that no step in the draft or the filing plan rests on an untested assumption about patent law or PTO practice.
applies_to: all applications; self-prepared and first-time filings
note: cannot be verified from documents — requires asking the drafter what they were unsure about and what they did

part_title: Threshold: is this patentable at all?
section: Setting up the patentability case in the draft
title: Run the statutory requirements before authorizing the filing
check: Verify the invention has been walked through statutory class, utility, novelty, and nonobviousness, with a recorded answer on each.
note: rollup of A01–A31: recording a yes/no/cannot-assess on §§ 101–103 is mechanical; whether to file is judgment

section: Was a search done at all
title: Confirm a patentability search preceded the decision to file
check: Verify that a documented patentability search of the invention exists and was completed before the decision to file this draft was made.
note: presence of a search record is mechanical; whether it preceded the filing decision is an intake fact

section: Was a search done at all
title: Test any decision to skip the search against documented coverage
check: If no search was made, verify the file records a reason that the relevant art is already known to the applicant with documented coverage — for example a field the applicant actually monitors, or an improvement already covered by an earlier search of the same concept.
note: the claimed field-newness or earlier-search justification comes only from the applicant

title: Verify the searcher was given every embodiment and the broad concept
check: Confirm the search request (or the DIY search plan) disclosed all embodiments, variations, and ramifications of the invention, and asked for the broad concept as well as the specific form.
note: a script can diff the spec's embodiments against the search request; coverage is adjudicated

title: Verify the search record states exactly what was searched
check: Confirm the search record identifies the classes, subclasses, keywords, and databases actually searched, plus any examiner consulted, and a searcher's restatement of the invention.
note: the four required sections are a presence check, but reading the searcher's restatement for a garbled feature is not

title: Confirm pre-grant published applications were searched, not just issued patents
check: Verify the search covered U.S. pre-grant application publications in the same classes and subclasses as the issued-patent search.

title: Confirm non-patent literature and foreign documents were covered
check: Verify the search extended beyond the U.S. patent database to non-patent literature and to foreign patent documents where the technology warrants it.

title: Grade the search by its source and discount for what cannot be searched
check: Verify that the confidence placed in the search matches the source used, and that the draft is not written as if the search were exhaustive.
note: who searched, for how long, and at what fee are intake facts

title: Confirm both a classification search and a keyword search were run
check: Verify the search record shows both a CPC classification search and a keyword/Boolean search, each used to check the other.
note: presence of both passes is mechanical; whether each checked the other is judgment

title: Confirm all plausible CPC codes, including analogous fields, were checked
check: Verify the classification search covered more than one CPC code and reached analogous arts, not just the single most obvious subclass.
note: counting CPC codes is mechanical; deciding whether analogous arts were reached is not

title: Confirm backward and forward citation chaining from the closest references
check: Verify that for each closely relevant reference the searcher followed its "References Cited" backward and its "Citing References" forward, and mined its "Field of Search" for further classes.

title: Check the database date coverage against the age of the technology
check: Verify that the databases searched actually reach back far enough to cover the era in which prior art for this technology would have been published.
applies_to: all applications; especially low-tech / long-established fields
note: tool coverage dates are fixed data; whether the technology could predate 1976 is a model call

title: Check the keyword set for synonyms, jargon, and pre-adoption terminology
check: Verify the recorded search terms include alternative words, technical jargon equivalents, wildcards, and the terminology that would have been used before the technology acquired its modern name.
note: a script can diff claim vocabulary against the recorded terms; synonym and jargon adequacy is judgment

title: Confirm each reference was read as a disclosure, not as a set of claims
check: Verify that the analysis of each close reference addressed its description and drawings, and did not conclude non-relevance because the reference's claims do not cover the invention.

title: Verify the effective date and document type of every cited reference
check: Confirm each reference's date and kind were correctly determined, including expired patents, patents effective as of their filing date, and pre-grant publications distinguished from granted patents.
note: kind codes and dates extract mechanically; classifying each reference's effective date correctly is judgment

title: Confirm the close references were studied in full, not screened from an abstract or single figure
check: Verify that every reference retained as relevant was obtained in full and analysed, rather than judged from an abstract page, a single Official Gazette figure, or a title.
note: a script can check a written summary exists per retained reference; depth of analysis is adjudicated

title: Confirm a written patentability analysis exists, run in the correct direction
check: Verify the file contains the applicant's own novelty and nonobviousness analysis against the closest references, listing the differences the invention has over the art — not the differences the art has over the invention — and addressing combinations of references.

section: Feeding the search back into the draft
title: Confirm the specification is aimed at the novel features and the closest art's deficiencies
check: Verify the draft specification recites and stresses the features found novel in the search, and explains their advantages against the deficiencies of the closest references.

section: Feeding the search back into the draft
title: Confirm claim scope was set by trial-and-error against the found art
check: Verify the independent claims recite the fewest/broadest features that both distinguish over the closest references under §102 and supply an unexpected result under §103 — and that the resulting scope is still worth filing on.

section: Feeding the search back into the draft
title: Confirm any teach-away reference found is preserved and used
check: Verify that references found in the search which teach away from the invention are identified in the file and reflected in the draft's discussion of unexpected results.

section: Feeding the search back into the draft
title: Confirm every material reference is queued for the Information Disclosure Statement
check: Verify that every relevant reference the search produced is on a list to be recorded in the PTO's file of this application, and that the search did not conclude with zero references.
note: set difference between the references in the search record and the IDS list, plus a citation-field completeness check

section: Feeding the search back into the draft
title: Confirm components referred to by name only are actually documented in the found prior art
check: Verify that each component the specification passes over by its well-known name — rather than describing and drawing it — is in fact already described in a prior-art publication located by the search.
note: drawings are needed because the tell is a named component with no figure and no prior-art citation

title: Discount and supplement the search for software and business-method inventions
check: For a software or business-method draft, verify the search went beyond the PTO patent database and that the claims are not resting on the absence of hits in it.

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Name every true inventor and only true inventors
check: Verify that the inventor list on the declaration/ADS contains every person who contributed an inventive concept and no one who did not.
note: who contributed what cannot be read off the papers — requires interviewing everyone who touched the project

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Test each named inventor against the one-claim contribution standard
check: Confirm that every named inventor contributed at least one inventive concept that is actually recited in at least one claim of the draft.
note: requires mapping each person's contribution onto claim limitations, which needs the contribution facts

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Strike builders, financiers, advisers, and honorary inventors
check: Confirm that no one is named merely for building/testing the invention, funding it, advising on business, or holding a title such as CTO or project lead.
applies_to: all applications, especially corporate and funded filings
note: requires asking whether any name comes from company convention rather than a claim contribution

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Re-verify inventorship against the final claim set and record each contribution
check: Confirm inventorship was re-reviewed after the last claim revision and that each inventor's specific contribution is written down and signed.
note: comparing the signed contribution statement's date against the last claim edit is mechanical; the re-verification is not

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Confirm documentation exists to defeat a later omitted-inventor claim
check: Verify that lab notebooks and signed consultant/contractor agreements exist for everyone who worked on the invention but is not named.
applies_to: all applications, especially where outside model makers or consultants were used
note: notebooks and consultant agreements are not filing documents — the applicant must produce them

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Identify the applicant correctly and separately from the inventors
check: Confirm the papers name the correct applicant (inventor, assignee, or obligated assignee) and that the applicant designation is consistent across the ADS, declaration, and any assignment.
note: consistency across ADS/declaration/assignment is cross-reference matching; the obligation-to-assign fact is intake

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Obtain a signed oath or declaration from every inventor
check: Verify that each named inventor has personally executed an oath or declaration, even where a company is the applicant.
note: count declarations against the inventor list and string-match names across ADS, declaration and assignment

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Test the invention against the inventor's employment agreement
check: Obtain each inventor's employment agreement and determine whether its assignment clause already captures this invention.
note: requires the executed employment agreement plus facts about when, where and with whose resources the invention was made

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Confirm the prior-inventions carve-out covers a pre-employment invention
check: If the inventor claims the invention predates the employment, verify it was disclosed on the prior-inventions list attached to the employment agreement.
note: requires the EA's prior-inventions schedule and corroboration of the claimed conception date

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Where there is no employment agreement, test employed-to-invent and shop rights
check: With no written EA, determine whether the inventor was hired or directed to make this invention, and whether company time, facilities, or materials were used.
applies_to: employed inventors with no written agreement
note: requires job description, assigned projects, and whose time, lab and materials were used

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Disclose gray-area inventions to the employer and obtain a written release before filing
check: Where the invention is within or near the scope of the employment agreement, verify the inventor disclosed it and holds a signed release before filing in their own name.
note: whether the invention was disclosed to the employer and a release obtained is an intake fact

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Put a Joint Owners' Agreement in place before filing
check: Where there will be two or more owners of the application, verify a signed Joint Owners' Agreement (or equivalent) exists stating shares, consent, and profit sharing.
note: if the agreement is produced a script can check for the required clauses; identifying the full owner set is intake

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Verify an executed, correctly completed assignment for every transfer of ownership
check: Where ownership is meant to sit anywhere other than with the inventors, confirm a signed assignment document exists with all particulars filled in.
severity: Fatal (where an assignee is the applicant or owner of record)
applies_to: all applications with an assignee, employed inventors, funded inventors
note: the assignment's required particulars are a field-completeness check; scope and payment structure need reading

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Prepare the assignment for prompt recording with the PTO
check: Confirm the assignment and its recordation cover sheet are ready to record, with the execution date of the application filled in if recording at filing.

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Confirm utility versus design is the right filing for this invention
check: Verify that what is novel about the invention matches the patent type being sought — function to utility, purely ornamental appearance to design.
applies_to: all applications, especially inventions with a distinctive shape
note: routed to the threshold gate: this is a patentability/vehicle question, not an ownership one

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Screen a design application against the PTO's design bars and format
check: For a design filing, verify the claimed design is not functional, not surface-only ornamentation, and not a natural shape — and that the papers are drawings plus a single formal claim.
note: routed to the threshold gate as a subject-matter eligibility and format question

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Confirm plant-patent eligibility and reproduction mode
check: For a plant invention, verify the plant is asexually reproducible and that a plant patent, not a utility patent or PVPA protection, is the right route.
note: how the plant reproduces is an intake fact; routed to the threshold gate

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
section: Subject matter that cannot be patented
title: Screen the claims against the judicial exceptions
check: Read each independent claim and confirm it does not recite a mathematical concept, a method of organizing human activity, a mental process, or another categorically excluded subject.
applies_to: all applications, especially software, business-method, diagnostic, and data-processing inventions
note: duplicates A02 from the 2019 PTO-guidelines angle; routed to the threshold gate

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
section: Subject matter that cannot be patented
title: Anchor software claims to changes in the physical world
check: For a software-implemented invention, verify the claims are directed to a process with real-world effects rather than to a computer program as such.
note: overlaps A03; routed to the threshold gate

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Confirm the fee set and entity status match the filing
check: Verify the correct filing/search/examination fees for the patent type are budgeted at the right entity status, and that maintenance-fee obligations are understood.
note: fee arithmetic is mechanical, but whether small/micro entity status is supportable is an intake fact

part_title: Inventorship, ownership, and the right to file
title: Check the applicant's expectations against what a patent actually does
check: Confirm the applicant understands the patent's term, that it confers no right to practice, and that it is not a defense against others' patents.
applies_to: all applications, especially self-represented and first-time filers
note: cannot be verified from documents at all — requires interviewing the applicant about their expectations

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify the PPA teaches how to make and use the invention
check: The PPA's description, standing alone, clearly teaches a person skilled in the field how to make and use the invention.

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify the best mode is disclosed
check: If the inventor currently prefers one version or mode of the invention, that preferred version is actually disclosed in the PPA.
applies_to: PPA only; also the regular application
note: the version the inventor currently prefers is an intake fact; a withheld best mode is invisible in the text alone

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify every embodiment you might later claim is described
check: The PPA describes all embodiments, variations, and ramifications the applicant might want to claim in the later regular application, including ones of doubtful operability.
note: the full set of embodiments the inventor can articulate must come from the inventor

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify drawings are present, understandable, and in permanent form
check: Drawings are included wherever they are needed to understand how to make and use the invention, and both drawings and text are in permanent (non-pencil) form.
note: figure and reference-numeral cross-checks are mechanical; legibility and permanence require looking at the sheets

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify the PPA is written to regular-application standard and in plain language
check: The PPA follows the format and quality of a regular application's specification and is written simply enough for a non-expert reader to follow.
note: section presence is mechanical; prose clarity is a model call

section: Auditing a draft PPA — disclosure sufficiency
title: Verify at least one claim is included in the PPA
check: The PPA contains at least one claim, even though claims are not legally required.
applies_to: PPA only; important where foreign priority is contemplated
note: presence of a claim is mechanical; testing whether the description supports every limitation is not

section: Auditing a draft PPA — formal papers, fees, and eligibility
title: Verify all required PPA papers are present and complete
check: The filing package contains every required part — description, drawings if needed, cover sheet, fee transmittal or electronic equivalent, micro-entity certification if claimed, ADS, and (for mail filings) a return receipt postcard.
note: inventory the package against the required-parts list

section: Auditing a draft PPA — formal papers, fees, and eligibility
title: Verify the fee is correct and the entity-status claim is truthful
check: The proper filing fee accompanies the PPA and any small-entity or micro-entity status asserted is actually supported for every named inventor.
applies_to: PPA only; same discipline applies to the regular application
note: per-inventor gross income, prior-patent counts and assignment obligations are intake facts

section: Auditing a draft PPA — formal papers, fees, and eligibility
title: Verify every contributor to the inventive subject matter is named in the PPA
check: All persons who contributed to the inventive subject matter disclosed in the PPA are named as inventors on it.
note: requires asking who supplied each alternative embodiment

section: Auditing a draft PPA — formal papers, fees, and eligibility
title: Verify the PPA is eligible subject matter and claims no earlier priority
check: The PPA is not directed to a design, and it contains no attempt to claim the benefit of any earlier domestic or foreign application.
note: blank benefit/priority sections are a mechanical check; design-vs-utility subject matter is not

section: Claiming priority from a PPA in a draft regular application
title: Verify every claim in the regular application is supported by the PPA disclosure
check: Each claim of the draft regular application is fully described — make-and-use level — in the PPA whose date is being claimed.
note: a script can enumerate claim limitations and retrieve candidate PPA passages; support is adjudicated

section: Claiming priority from a PPA in a draft regular application
title: Verify post-PPA changes and improvements are properly captured
check: Any change or improvement made to the invention after the PPA was filed is either covered by a subsequent PPA or carried into the regular application with no expectation of the earlier date.
note: a text diff is mechanical; what changed since the PPA and what counts as new matter is not

section: Claiming priority from a PPA in a draft regular application
title: Verify inventor overlap between the PPA and the regular application
check: At least one inventor named in the PPA is also named in the regular application, and that inventor's invention is both claimed in the regular application and fully disclosed in the PPA.
note: the name overlap is a set intersection; the claimed-and-disclosed half is judgment

section: Claiming priority from a PPA in a draft regular application
title: Verify the regular application actually claims the benefit of the PPA
check: The draft regular application contains an express reference claiming the benefit of the PPA's filing date.
note: presence of the benefit statement in the ADS and specification plus a serial-number and date match

section: Claiming priority from a PPA in a draft regular application
title: Verify each PPA relied on was filed within the preceding year, and map inventions to PPAs
check: Where the regular application claims benefit of more than one PPA, every one of them was filed within the year preceding the regular application's filing date, and each invention claimed is traced to a PPA that discloses it.
applies_to: Applications claiming priority from multiple PPAs
note: the one-year window is date arithmetic; mapping each claim to a PPA that discloses it is not

section: The 12-month deadline, foreign rights, and publication
title: Verify the regular application will be filed within one year of the PPA
check: The regular application's projected filing date falls within twelve months of the PPA's filing date, with margin.
note: pure date arithmetic from the PPA filing-receipt date against the target filing date

section: The 12-month deadline, foreign rights, and publication
title: Verify the foreign filing decision is made inside the PPA year
check: Any foreign or PCT filing that is to claim the PPA's priority is scheduled within one year of the PPA's filing date, and non-Convention countries are addressed before any publication or public sale.
applies_to: Applications claiming PPA priority where foreign rights are wanted
note: whether foreign rights are wanted, and in which jurisdictions, is an intake fact

section: The 12-month deadline, foreign rights, and publication
title: Verify the Nonpublication Request decision is made at the time of filing
check: The applicant has consciously decided whether to file a Nonpublication Request with the regular application, understanding that publication runs from the PPA's date.
applies_to: Applications claiming PPA priority; all applications where trade secret status matters
note: the 18-month date runs mechanically from the PPA; the trade-secret and foreign-filing intent behind the decision is intake

title: Verify a signed, dated, and witnessed record of conception exists
check: There is a written record of conception, in permanent form, signed and dated by the inventor and signed and dated by two witnesses who attest they witnessed and understood it.
applies_to: All applications, especially where derivation or disputed inventorship is a live risk
note: the conception record is not a filing document — the inventor must produce it; signature, date and witness lines are then checkable

title: Verify the witnesses are competent, impartial, and not potential coinventors
check: Each witness on the conception or building-and-testing record is technically able to understand the invention, is impartial, and actually read and understood the subject matter rather than merely witnessing a signature.
applies_to: All applications relying on witnessed records
note: requires knowing each witness's relationship to the inventor and technical competence

title: Verify the conception record captures ramifications and novel features
check: The conception record or Invention Disclosure covers title, purpose, description, sketch, ramifications, possible novel features, closest known prior art, and advantages — not just the core embodiment.
applies_to: All applications; conception and Invention Disclosure records

title: Reject sealed-envelope and computer-only records as proof
check: The file does not rely on a mailed-to-self sealed envelope or on purely electronic records to establish conception; anything created on a computer has been printed and signed.
applies_to: All applications relying on documentation of conception
note: requires asking the inventor directly what they believe secures their date

title: Verify pre-filing disclosures were made under a signed NDA
check: Every person or organization shown the invention before filing — model makers, machine shops, consultants, prospective partners — signed a Nondisclosure Agreement, and the transactions are documented.
applies_to: All applications, for disclosures made before the PPA or regular application was filed
note: the pre-filing disclosure history and the NDAs covering it come only from the applicant

title: Confirm no pre-filing disclosure has already killed foreign rights
check: Verify that the invention was not published, sold, or otherwise publicly disclosed before the U.S. filing date, because most foreign countries have no grace period.
applies_to: all applications where foreign rights may be wanted
note: the disclosure timeline comes only from the inventor; comparing it against the filing date is then mechanical

title: File in non-Convention countries before any publication or sale
check: Verify that, if any non-Convention (non-treaty) country is on the target list, filings there are scheduled before the invention or the application becomes publicly known.
applies_to: applications with foreign filing intent in non-Convention jurisdictions
note: target jurisdictions and the PCT plan are intake facts; the publication-clock arithmetic is mechanical

title: Test the commercial case for each foreign country before committing
check: Verify that a documented commercial justification exists for every country on the foreign-filing list, rather than an untested belief that the invention will "capture the world."
note: commercial justification per country cannot be assessed from documents at all

title: Diary the one-year Paris Convention deadline at filing
check: Verify that a calendar entry exists for one year from the earliest U.S. filing date (the PPA date if a PPA was filed), by which a PCT application or direct Convention filings must be on file.
applies_to: all applications where foreign rights may be wanted
note: identifying the priority anchor and computing the date is mechanical; confirming foreign intent and that it is diarised is not

title: Diary the 30-month PCT national-stage deadline — no reminder will come
check: Verify that a 30-month-from-priority calendar reminder is set for entering the national stage in each designated PCT jurisdiction, with the applicant on notice that no office will remind them.
note: the 30-month computation is mechanical; PCT intent and the docketing evidence are intake

title: Set the decision point two to three months before each deadline
check: Verify that the foreign-filing *decision* is diarised two to three months ahead of the legal deadline, not on the deadline itself.

section: Foreign filing licence and the six-month rule
title: Do not file abroad before the foreign-filing licence or six months elapse
check: Verify that no foreign filing is planned or already made before the PTO grants a foreign-filing licence or six months have run from the U.S. filing date.
applies_to: all applications with foreign filing intent
note: the licence line on the filing receipt is a presence check; the foreign-filing plan is intake

section: Foreign filing licence and the six-month rule
title: Flag military or dual-use subject matter for secrecy-order exposure
check: Verify whether the disclosed subject matter has possible military or national-security applications, in which case no foreign-filing licence will issue and a secrecy order may follow.
applies_to: applications disclosing defense, cryptographic, or dual-use technology
note: requires reading past the commercial framing to the underlying dual-use technology

title: Do not file a nonpublication request if foreign filing is contemplated
check: Verify that the decision to include or omit a Nonpublication Request in the filing papers is consistent with the applicant's actual foreign-filing intent.
note: presence of the NPR is mechanical; consistency with the applicant's actual foreign-filing intent is not

title: Record the 45-day NPR rescission obligation with the foreign-filing diary
check: Verify that, where an NPR is being filed, the file records the duty to rescind it within 45 days of any foreign filing, including a PCT filing.
applies_to: applications filed with a Nonpublication Request
note: conditional on an NPR being filed; the 45-day trigger must be recorded against the foreign-filing diary

title: Consider a second claim set for central-claiming jurisdictions
check: Verify that the claim set has been reviewed against the different claiming conventions of the intended foreign jurisdictions, and that a second claim set is contemplated for a PCT filing where appropriate.
applies_to: applications with foreign filing intent, especially European
note: target jurisdictions are an intake fact

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Confirm the draft is the right kind of child application
check: Verify that the draft is characterized correctly — continuation, divisional, CIP, independent, or substitute — against what it actually claims relative to the parent.
applies_to: continuations, divisionals, CIPs, independent and substitute applications
note: a paragraph-level diff against the parent is mechanical; classifying the result as continuation/divisional/CIP is judgment

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Verify the parent is still pending on the intended filing date
check: Verify that the parent application is still pending — neither abandoned nor issued — as of the date this child application will actually be filed.
note: status and date comparison of the parent against the planned filing date

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Flag a refiling of an abandoned case as a substitute with no priority benefit
check: Verify whether the draft is in substance a refiling of an application that was already abandoned, in which case it gets no benefit of the earlier filing date.
note: the abandonment-vs-filing date test is mechanical; the gap-period prior-art assessment is not

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Check the divisional's claims are confined to the divided-out invention and add no new matter
check: Verify that a divisional's claims are directed solely to the nonelected invention and that its specification adds nothing that was not in the parent.
note: the specification diff is mechanical; whether each claim belongs to the divided-out invention is judgment

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Verify the cross-reference and continuity data recite the complete chain
check: Verify that the CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS paragraph and the ADS continuity data name every application in the priority chain, with correct serial numbers, filing dates, and continuity types.
applies_to: continuations, divisionals, CIPs, and any application claiming domestic benefit
note: serial numbers and dates cross-reference mechanically; the correctness of each relationship word does not

section: Choosing the right kind of related application
title: Check inventorship against the child's claims
check: Verify that the named inventors match the claims actually presented in the child application, which may differ in scope from the parent's.
note: who conceived the CIP's newly added matter is an intake fact

section: New matter and priority in a CIP
title: Identify the CIP's new matter and mark which claims lose the parent's date
check: Verify that every element of new matter in the CIP is identified, and that each claim is mapped to the earliest date its support actually justifies.
note: a script can pair each limitation with candidate parent passages; entitlement to the parent date is adjudicated

section: New matter and priority in a CIP
title: Screen a CIP for transition-application status before adding claims to new matter
check: Verify whether the CIP claims priority to an application filed before March 16, 2013, and if so whether any claim requires support from matter added in the CIP.
applies_to: CIPs claiming priority to pre-March 16, 2013 applications
note: the March 16 2013 date test is mechanical; the per-claim support audit that triggers it is not

title: Run a double-patenting check across the whole family before filing
check: Verify that the claims of this application are patentably distinct from the claims of every other pending application and issued patent owned by the same applicant.
applies_to: related-application families; any second case on the same invention

title: Decide whether a terminal disclaimer will be needed, and check common ownership
check: Verify whether the child's claims are patentably different from the parent's, and if not, that a terminal disclaimer is planned and both cases will remain commonly owned.
applies_to: continuations and CIPs where the parent will issue
note: whether both cases will stay commonly owned is an intake fact

title: Confirm whether a restriction requirement actually supports a voluntary divisional
check: Verify that the divisional follows an examiner's restriction requirement, or, if voluntary, that its claims are to a clearly different invention.
note: locating the restriction requirement in the parent file history is mechanical; matching claims to the nonelected group is not

title: Ask whether the benefit claim is worth the shortened term
check: Verify that the decision to claim benefit of the parent's filing date was made deliberately, weighing the 20-year term measured from the parent rather than from this application.

title: Verify the specification enables a skilled artisan to make and use the invention
check: Confirm the specification describes the invention in full, clear, concise, and exact terms sufficient for a person of ordinary skill in the field to build and use a working version without undue effort.

title: Verify critical or unusual dimensions, materials, and component values are disclosed
check: Confirm that any dimension, material, or component value that is critical to performance or at all unusual is stated in the specification, rather than left to the reader.
note: only the inventor can confirm which parameters are actually critical to performance

title: Verify exotic materials and components identify a source or how to make them
check: Confirm that every uncommon material, component, or manufacturing step is accompanied by a supplier identification or a reference explaining how to obtain or perform it.
applies_to: all applications (especially chemical and process inventions)
note: Serious but uncurable: a missing source or recipe cannot be added post-filing

title: Verify trademarked ingredients are described by composition or generic equivalent
check: Confirm that any component identified only by a trademark is also described by its composition or a generic name plus manufacturer, and that the invention does not depend on the trademark alone.
applies_to: chemical | all applications using proprietary materials
note: script can list brand names and TM/R symbols; model must judge whether the mark is the only disclosure of a critical ingredient

title: Verify components that do not yet exist are fully designed, described, and drawn
check: Confirm that every element the invention requires but which cannot be purchased off the shelf is itself designed out in the specification and shown in the drawings.
note: needs the sheets to confirm the non-existent component actually has its own figure

title: Verify the disclosure is complete because nothing can be added after filing
check: Confirm the draft contains every technical detail and ramification the inventor currently knows, because no new matter may be added once the application is on file.
note: cannot be answered from the draft alone; requires the inventor's notes, sketches and data to know what is missing

title: Verify special deposit and sequence-listing obligations for biological subject matter
check: Confirm that any not-widely-available biological material is deposited in an approved depository and that nucleotide or amino acid sequences are provided as a separate, rule-compliant sequence listing.
note: whether a biological material is obtainable and whether a deposit was made are facts only the applicant supplies

section: Written description, drawings, and claim support
title: Verify every claim element appears in a figure and in the description
check: Walk each claim element by element and confirm each recited element is both shown in a drawing figure and described in the specification text.
note: script can build the claim-term/spec-paragraph table; model must catch terminology drift and confirm figure depiction

section: Written description, drawings, and claim support
title: Verify ramifications and alternative embodiments are disclosed
check: Confirm the specification describes alternative materials, sizes, shapes, uses, process variations, and additional embodiments rather than a single implementation.
note: probing the inventor for unwritten variants is part of the check; ramifications cannot be added after filing

section: Written description, drawings, and claim support
title: Verify a flowchart is provided for every process aspect of the invention
check: Confirm that computer, chemical, or mechanical processes are shown as a flowchart with each separate step in its own labeled block, in addition to the narrative description.
note: script can detect method claims and whether a flowchart figure is listed; block granularity needs a model

section: Written description, drawings, and claim support
title: Verify block diagrams explain every nonconventional block
check: Confirm that each block in a block diagram is either a standard, conventional part or is backed by a schematic, a clear explanation, or a literature reference.
note: deciding which blocks are conventional is domain judgment over the actual diagrams

section: Written description, drawings, and claim support
title: Verify drawing formalities: prior-art labeling, separate filing, and every novel feature shown
check: Confirm any prior-art figure is labeled "Prior Art" and described in the Background, the drawings are a separate document from the specification, and enough views exist to show every novel feature.
note: visual properties of the sheets; the claimed-feature coverage half is already blocking via E08/G29

title: Verify no embodiment is singled out as "best" or "preferred"
check: Confirm the draft discloses all known modes fully but nowhere designates one as the best mode or the preferred embodiment.
note: script greps preferred/best/optimal; model must also judge the converse tell of unequal embodiment depth

title: Verify the description is clear, precise, and free of ambiguity
check: Confirm the specification is written in short, clear sentences with no vague, ambiguous, or unintelligible passages, and that terminology is used consistently.

section: Statements that could narrow or invalidate the patent
title: Verify the draft contains no self-limiting statements
check: Confirm the application contains no statement a court could use to limit the claims — no "objects," no "the invention" phrasing, no essentiality statements, no unearned advantages.
note: script produces the candidate phrase list; model decides which are genuine disclaimers

section: Statements that could narrow or invalidate the patent
title: Verify no negative, restrictive, or wishy-washy statements are present
check: Confirm the draft never says a novel part resembles something known, that novelty resides solely in one part, that something "might" work, or that anything is always better, necessary, or not done a certain way.
note: hedges and negatives are greppable; whether a comparison is an admission is a model call

section: Statements that could narrow or invalidate the patent
title: Verify the Background contains no inventive concepts
check: Confirm the Background section discusses only known problems and genuine prior art, with none of the applicant's own inventive concepts described there.

section: Statements that could narrow or invalidate the patent
title: Verify advantages are factual, verified against the prior art, and tied to embodiments
check: Confirm every advantage asserted is a real advantage over the prior art, is exhibited by at least one disclosed embodiment, and is framed nonlimitingly as an advantage of embodiments rather than of "the invention."
note: testing an asserted advantage against the art requires the references, not just the draft

section: Software, computer-related inventions, and business methods
title: Verify a program listing or an adequately detailed flowchart is included
check: Confirm any software, firmware, or microprocessor-based invention discloses either a source/object code listing or a flowchart detailed enough for an ordinarily skilled programmer to write and debug the program.

section: Software, computer-related inventions, and business methods
title: Verify the specification ties the process to hardware for subject-matter eligibility
check: Confirm the specification describes the machine or apparatus and the relationship between the claimed process and that hardware, so the claims are hardware-based rather than abstract.
note: spec-side support for eligibility; the claim-side 101 test is G30/G31

section: Software, computer-related inventions, and business methods
title: Verify implementation instructions for the program are in the specification
check: Confirm the specification explains how to implement the listing — programming language, target processor, how the program controls the machine, and the input/output hardware to connect.
note: Serious but uncurable: implementation detail cannot be added after filing

section: Software, computer-related inventions, and business methods
title: Verify the disclosed program works and is submitted in the required format
check: Confirm any included program listing is free of serious bugs and complies with the PTO's submission format rules for its length and filing route.
note: line counts and ASCII/format rules are scriptable; whether the listing actually runs is an inventor fact

title: Verify the specification follows Rule 77 section order and headings
check: Confirm the specification's sections appear in the PTO's prescribed order with capitalized headings, and that inapplicable sections are either omitted or marked "not applicable."
note: Rule 77 section presence, order, capitalized headings and the claims page break are deterministic; the substance of the cross-reference is F05

title: Verify the title, Summary, and Abstract meet their content and length limits
check: Confirm the title is meaningful and within 500 characters, the Summary paraphrases the claimed embodiments, and the Abstract is 150 words or less and summarizes the entire technical content.
note: abstract word count and the 500-character title limit are scriptable; whether the Summary tracks the claims needs a model

title: Verify the Conclusion includes a broadening paragraph
check: Confirm the specification ends with a Conclusion that restates the advantages, describes alternative forms and uses, and adds an express broadening paragraph.
note: presence of the Conclusion heading is scriptable; whether a real broadening paragraph is there is a model call

title: Verify the filing packet is complete and signed
check: Confirm all required formal papers accompany the specification — transmittal, fee payment, signed Patent Application Declaration, Application Data Sheet, Information Disclosure Statement, drawings, and a Nonpublication Request if applicable.
note: form inventory is a checklist against the packet; the nonpublication-request decision turns on foreign-filing intent

title: Verify the application does not combine unrelated inventions or inventors
check: Confirm that any multiple inventions covered in the one application are genuinely related and share the same inventive entity.
note: needs the declaration/ADS inventor list plus who actually contributed to which claimed subject

title: Provide a complete set of figures covering every claimed feature
check: Verify the draft's figures show every feature the claims recite or will recite, in perspective/isometric views, with any prior-art figure labeled and the drawings kept as a document separate from the specification text.
note: script enumerates claim elements; model must locate each in the figures. Views cannot be added post-filing

title: Enforce reference-numeral and labeling hygiene on the drawings
check: Verify each unique part has its own numeral, the same part carries the same numeral in every figure, numerals are even and start above the highest figure number, lead lines have no arrowheads, and no numeral designates a whole figure.
note: numeral-to-part table and the even/above-highest-figure rules are scriptable from the spec; arrowheads, circled numerals and dimensions are visual

title: Supply an enabling flowchart or program listing for software and process inventions
check: Verify that any software, computer-implemented, chemical, or mechanical process disclosure includes a flowchart figure or program listing plus a written explanation detailed enough that a skilled practitioner needs only routine skill to implement it.
applies_to: software/business method; chemical, mechanical, and computer processes

title: Test the title for both over-narrowness and emptiness
check: Verify the title captures the essence of the invention, is 500 characters or fewer, and is neither narrower than the full scope of the disclosed embodiments nor so broad as to be meaningless.
note: character count is scriptable; over-narrow vs meaningless is a model judgment against the embodiments

title: Verify the cross-reference paragraph and the limits of incorporation by reference
check: Verify that every PPA, parent, or technically related application the draft relies on is recited in the Cross-Reference section in benefit-claim form, and that no matter essential to enablement or claim support is left outside the application and merely incorporated by reference.
note: needs the filing history and the earlier applications themselves; a missing benefit claim forfeits the date and incorporated essential matter cannot be pulled in later

title: Confirm the Technical Field describes the field, not the invention
check: Verify the Technical Field section states a preexisting field at two levels of generality and does not describe the invention itself.
note: failure mode is an admission that the invention is part of the preexisting field

title: Confirm the Background never describes the invention or its advantages
check: Verify the Background/Prior Art section contains no description of the applicant's invention and no statement of its advantages.

title: Confirm each prior-art reference is fully cited and factually knocked
check: Verify every prior-art approach discussed is identified with inventor/author name, number or publication and page, and date, and is criticized in factual — not opinionated — terms.
note: script can check each citation for name/number/date; verifying the knock is factual needs the references

title: Scrub the Background for admissions and excess detail
check: Verify the Background does not admit that the problem was already recognized in the art, does not describe the prior-art device in enough detail to isolate the applicant's changes, and runs no longer than a few paragraphs.
note: whether the problem was actually recognized in the art is a fact from the inventor

title: Confirm advantages are attributed to "one or more aspects" and each is actually delivered
check: Verify the Advantages narrative avoids the words "invention" and "objects", attributes benefits to "one or more aspects" or "some embodiments", and lists no advantage that is not fulfilled by at least one disclosed aspect.
note: script greps 'invention'/'object' subjects; model must check each advantage is delivered by a disclosed aspect

title: Confirm the Summary paraphrases every claim and states no object of the invention
check: Verify the Summary gives a broad overview plus text paraphrasing each of the claims, does not focus on a single embodiment, and never recites an "object of the invention".
note: 'object of the invention' is greppable; matching each claim to a paraphrase needs a model

title: Confirm the Brief Description of Drawings is one short sentence per figure with no numerals
check: Verify each figure has its own short descriptive sentence and that the section contains no reference numerals, part-level detail, or operational description.
note: sentence-per-figure count and reference-numeral detection are scriptable; creeping part-level detail needs a model

title: Confirm a List of Reference Numerals exists and reconciles both ways with the drawings
check: Verify a separately headed list of reference numerals and part names is present and that every numeral on the drawings appears in the specification and every numeral in the specification appears on the drawings.
note: presence of the list plus two-way reconciliation between spec text and the List of Reference Numerals is deterministic; numerals visible only on the sheets fall to F02

title: Confirm static structure is described separately from operation, general before specific
check: Verify the Detailed Description describes the static physical structure of each embodiment in its own section, before and separate from the section describing how it operates, and moves from overall parts to details.

title: Confirm every part, every interconnection, and every claim term is described
check: Verify each part shown in the drawings is described, each part-to-part connection or mounting is expressly stated, and every term that appears in the claims appears first in the specification.
note: literal claim-term presence is scriptable; every-part and every-interconnection coverage needs a model

title: Confirm consistent part naming and correct use of "a" and "the"
check: Verify each part is introduced once with alternative equivalent names and an indefinite article, then referred to by a single consistent name with the definite article thereafter.
note: script builds the name-per-numeral index and flags first-use articles; model adjudicates equivalent-name introductions

title: Confirm nothing has been held back: dimensions, materials, relationships, and sources of supply
check: Verify that every exotic, special, or critical part is described with its dimensions, exemplary materials, relationships, and sources of supply, with nothing withheld as a trade secret.
note: detecting a deliberate trade-secret withholding requires asking the inventor

title: Confirm every specific is stated in nonlimiting terms with alternatives
check: Verify each stated dimension, material, shape, or value is framed as what is presently contemplated for that embodiment, accompanied by alternatives, with ranges stating whether endpoints are included.
note: script can find flat declaratives about materials/dimensions and ranges with no endpoint statement; model judges sufficiency of the alternatives

title: Confirm technical terms are defined and a glossary is supplied for complex inventions
check: Verify every sophisticated or technical term used in the draft is defined in plain language, and that a reasonably complex invention carries a glossary section with broad definitions.
applies_to: all applications; especially computer, biotech, electronic, chemical, medical, and complex mechanical

title: Confirm trademarks are replaced by generic terms or properly identified
check: Verify trademarked products are referred to by generic name where the mark is not needed for identification, and that any mark actually used is capitalized, identified as a mark, used as an adjective with a generic noun, and attributed to its owner.
applies_to: all applications; especially chemical and materials
note: script flags brand names and checks the four formalities; whether a generic substitute exists is a model call

title: Confirm the reader always knows which figure is under discussion
check: Verify each technical discussion is tied to a named figure, that the text handles roughly one figure at a time, and that any part mentioned but not drawn is expressly flagged as not shown.
note: script finds technical passages with no Fig. citation and parts lacking a '(not shown)' tag; needs the sheets to know what is actually drawn

title: Confirm the Operation section covers every part's function and introduces none
check: Verify the Operation section describes the working of the whole system and then of every individual part by name and numeral, introduces no part or numeral not already introduced in the description, and stresses advantages without stating limitations.
note: numeral diff between Operation and Detailed Description is scriptable both ways; whether every part's function is explained is a model call

title: Confirm all important embodiments are described and none is labeled "preferred"
check: Verify the draft describes, draws, and claims every reasonably important embodiment, each with its own structure-then-operation treatment, and that no embodiment is called "preferred", "main", or "the invention".
note: 'preferred'/'main'/'the present invention' are greppable; the embodiment-coverage half needs the inventor's list and cannot be cured after filing

title: Confirm a comprehensive ramifications passage sweeps every element through every variation
check: Verify the ramifications passage walks each element of the device or method and states whether it can be eliminated, duplicated, resized, remade in a different material, shape, or color, connected differently, given a different mode of operation, or made integrally versus separately.
note: the eight variation axes must be swept element by element; ramifications cannot be added post-filing

title: Confirm the Conclusion restates advantages and cedes scope to the claims
check: Verify a Conclusion, Ramifications, and Scope section exists at the end of the specification that restates the advantages in embodiment terms, lists remaining alternatives, and states that scope is determined by the claims and their legal equivalents rather than by the illustrated embodiments.
note: section presence and the claims-control sentence are scriptable; absolute-vs-comparative advantage language needs a model

title: Confirm the abstract is a single nonlimiting paragraph of 150 words or fewer
check: Verify the abstract is one paragraph of no more than 150 words on its own page after the claims (and after any sequence listing), free of throat-clearing phrases and of "the invention", with a reference numeral in parentheses after each named part.
note: 150-word count, single paragraph, placement and throat-clearing/'the invention' greps are scriptable; 'nonlimiting' is a model judgment

title: Purge patent profanity and self-limiting statements
check: Verify the specification contains none of the listed "patent profanity" words, never refers to "the invention", and contains no negative, restrictive, wishy-washy, or absolute statements an adversary could use to narrow or invalidate the patent.
note: the patent-profanity word list is a literal grep; each hit and the semantic failures need model adjudication

title: Enforce writing mechanics and heading discipline
check: Verify the draft uses short sentences, copious descriptive headings, plain non-legal language, active voice, a noun before every reference numeral, and clean grammar, spelling, and punctuation.
note: sentence/paragraph length, heading density, bare numerals and 'said'/'means' in the spec are scriptable; grammar and voice need a model

title: Confirm the draft has been re-read and checked by an independent reader
check: Verify the draft has been set aside, re-reviewed against the completeness and non-limiting standards, and read by a trusted third party who confirmed it teaches how to make and use the invention and does not limit it.
note: whether a second reader actually reviewed the draft is a process fact, not a property of the text

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Confirm at least one independent claim exists and is the broadest claim
check: Verify the draft contains at least one independent claim that stands alone and defines a complete, operative invention, and that it is drafted to be as broad as the prior art permits.
note: script confirms a claim set exists and identifies the independents; whether the lead claim is as broad as the art permits needs the search plus a model

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Provide alternative independent claims of different statutory types plus dependent backup
check: Verify the claim set includes more than one independent claim, drafted in different forms (apparatus, means, method) where the invention admits, each followed by dependent claims reciting the significant additional features.
note: script counts and classifies independents by preamble and counts their dependents; whether the alternatives are genuinely different needs a model

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Do not rely on a dependent claim to cover a feature standing alone
check: Verify the draft does not depend on a dependent claim to protect an important feature *per se*, since a dependent claim covers that feature only in combination with everything in its parent.
note: depends on which features the inventor most wants to own

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Check claim numbering, ordering, and physical layout against Rule 75
check: Verify claims are numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals, the least restrictive claim is claim 1, dependent claims are grouped with the claims they refer to, elements are set off by line indentation, and the claims begin on their own page.
note: consecutive numbering, dependent grouping/ordering, hanging indents and the claims page break are deterministic; whether claim 1 is truly the broadest is G33's call

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Avoid multiple dependent claims and an unjustified claim count
check: Verify no claim refers in the alternative to more than one preceding claim, and that the total number of claims is justified by the complexity of the invention with the claims differing substantially from each other.
note: multiple-dependency detection and the count thresholds are scriptable, but a script would false-pass a padded set of near-identical dependents

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Check claim punctuation, capitalization, and forbidden characters
check: Verify each claim has one capital letter (the first word), one period (at the end), and contains no dashes, quotation marks, parentheses in the body, trademarks, or unexpanded abbreviations.
note: one capital, one period, no dashes/quotes/parentheses/abbreviations; the single-capital rule also catches trademarks used as element names

section: Claim set architecture and formal requirements
title: Check that every claim has a proper preamble in a statutory class, and avoid Jepson form
check: Verify each independent claim opens with a preamble that names its statutory class or gives a title/purpose for the whole unit, and that the draft does not use the Jepson "wherein the improvement comprises" format.
note: Jepson markers are greppable and a statutory-class preamble matches a fixed vocabulary; a title-style preamble must be judged

title: Verify correct use of "a," "said," and "the," and distinct names for distinct elements
check: Verify each element is introduced with "a," referred back to with "said" using exactly the same words, and that different elements of the same kind are named "first"/"second" rather than repeated.
note: script lists first vs later appearances of each noun phrase; model decides which repeats are genuinely different elements

title: Hunt for missing antecedents
check: Verify that every "said X" in every claim has an earlier recitation of "X" in exactly the same words, within that claim or an available parent claim.
note: archetype: script lists every 'said X' with no identical earlier 'a X' up the dependency chain; model separates inherent-property references from real missing antecedents

title: Flag vague, casual, and unanchored relative terms
check: Verify the claims contain no unexpanded abbreviations and no vague or relative terms ("large," "small," "close," "strong," "suitable," "standard," "sufficient") unless anchored to a reference or clearly understood by a person having ordinary skill in the art.
note: degree words and unexpanded abbreviations are greppable; whether a PHOSITA would understand the term is a model call

title: Check for prolixity — excess wordiness
check: Verify each claim uses the minimum number of words needed to delineate the essence of the invention, with roughly one clause per necessary part.
note: clause count versus numeraled parts is a scriptable signal; prolixity itself is a judgment

title: Verify every element is affirmatively recited as the subject of its own clause
check: Verify each significant element is introduced positively (normally with "a") as the subject of its own clause, and that no function is recited before the element that performs it has been affirmatively recited.
note: script can flag possessives and participial clauses that introduce a noun; model confirms the element is smuggled in

title: Verify each element is followed only by its own shape or function
check: Verify no element recitation is immediately followed by the function of a *different* element.
note: deciding whose function a trailing modifier describes is pure comprehension

title: Verify every recited operation has enough structure behind it
check: Verify that any operation, movement, or result recited in a claim is attributed to structure adequate to perform it, or is expressed as a means clause.
applies_to: all applications; especially mechanical and electromechanical
note: whether the recited hardware could plausibly perform the recited operation is domain judgment

title: Replace negative limitations with positive ones
check: Verify the claims recite what the invention is rather than what it is not, and contain no negative limitations that make a claim unclear or awkward.
note: negatives are greppable; the holes/recesses exception and restatability need a model

title: Audit the connective expressions "and" and "or"
check: Verify each use of "and" and "or" in a claim has one unambiguous meaning, with "and" reserved for necessary structure and alternatives handled cleanly.
note: script finds clauses mixing 'and' with 'or'; ambiguity and the Markush question are model calls

title: Verify each claim recites a complete, operative assemblage
check: Verify each claim, standing alone, recites enough elements to define a working, complete device or process consistent with what is recognized as a unit in its art.

title: Verify all elements interconnect and cooperate (no aggregation)
check: Verify every element recited in a claim is logically related and physically or functionally connected to the other elements, and that the combination cooperates toward a common end.
note: script can list elements never named in an interconnection clause; aggregation is a substantive judgment

title: Flag elements claimed by result or function instead of structure
check: Verify no claim element is defined solely by the advantage, function, or result it produces without reciting structure or a means/device clause.

title: Check for prohibited single-means claims
check: Verify that any claim using "means" language recites a combination of two or more elements, not a single means.
